name: How Do You Fix a Driveway That Drains Toward the Garage?

mainEntity.name: Can a driveway contractor fix a sloped driveway that drains toward the garage?
mainEntity.text: Can a driveway contractor fix a sloped driveway that drains toward the garage?

acceptedAnswer.text: A driveway that drains toward the garage is a design and grading problem, not just a surface problem. A contractor may need to re-slope the driveway, change the pitch near the garage, install drainage channels or trench drains, or rebuild the base so water flows away from the structure. Simply patching cracks or applying a new surface will not solve repeated water intrusion if the grade is wrong. In Los Angeles County, drainage is especially important because runoff can create slipping hazards, foundation moisture concerns, and staining. Homeowners should ask the contractor how the new design will move water during heavy rain, where runoff will exit, and whether the work will affect the sidewalk or adjacent landscaping. A good solution should be based on site measurements and elevations, not guesswork. If the contractor cannot explain the drainage plan clearly, the problem may return after the next storm.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but the fix usually requires more than resurfacing. A contractor may need to regrade the driveway, adjust the slope, add drainage channels, or rebuild sections of the base so water moves away from the garage. If the slope problem is ignored, new concrete or paving can fail again quickly.
